question: At the end of which of the following Five-year plans of India, five IITs were set up in the country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Five IITs** were set up in India at the end of the **First Five-Year Plan**.
 
• The first IIT, **IIT Kharagpur**, was established in 1951.
 
• This was followed by the establishment of IITs at Bombay (Mumbai), Madras (Chennai), Kanpur, and Delhi in subsequent years.
 
• The establishment of these institutes was aimed at creating a pool of highly trained engineers and technologists to support India’s industrial development.
 
• The IITs have since grown to become premier institutions of higher learning in engineering and technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** of India was launched in 1951 and focused on the agricultural sector to address the food shortages.
 
• It was based on the Harrod-Domar model and aimed to increase productivity in agriculture, improve infrastructure, and achieve self-sufficiency in food production.
 
• The success of the First Five-Year Plan laid the foundation for future economic planning in India.
 
• The establishment of IITs underlined the emphasis on technical education and research in India's development strategy.
